## TECH STOCKS RECOVER
Nvidia rose 2.2% and Meta [(META.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/META.O) climbed almost 2%.

Advanced Micro Devices [(AMD.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/AMD.O) rose 4.9% ‌after Raymond ⁠James upgraded the stock.

On the Nasdaq, 3,059 stocks rose and 1,740 fell as advancing issues ⁠outnumbered decliners ​by a 1.76-to-1 ratio.

- Nvidia results to offer read on AI sentiment
- Dick's Sporting slides after cutting annual forecasts
- Moderna surges after Barclays target price hike
- US consumer confidence falls to seven-month low in August

NEW YORK, Aug 25 (Reuters) - Wall Street's ​main indexes closed higher on Tuesday, as technology stocks recovered from a selloff ahead of AI heavyweight Nvidia's results, while investors found ‌some relief in drops in oil prices and bond yields.

The gains could ease investor concerns sparked by a [recent bond market rout](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/selling-grips-bond-markets-us-japan-inflation-fiscal-worries-take-hold-2026-08-18/) that lifted yields and pressured equities. They could also help set the tone for September, a historically weaker month for stocks.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

Longer-dated Treasury yields fell on Tuesday as oil prices dropped to a one-week low and traders continued to weigh the implications ​of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's decision to expand Treasury buybacks.

"There's a lot of push and pull — in the bond market, geopolitics, oil," said ​Joe Quinlan, head of market strategy for Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank.

"But we're pretty constructive on the outlook (for ⁠the) next 12, 18 months on the U.S. economy; therefore, we are constructive on the markets as well."

Nvidia's [(NVDA.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/NVDA.O) results on Wednesday will be the next test ​for the earnings-driven rally. Any signs of slowing growth could reignite concerns about stretched valuations and how long the AI boom can sustain them.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

"This is the ​classic problem of being the epicenter of the buildout — when you are the trade, execution stops being a catalyst and becomes a prerequisite," said Mark Malek, chief investment officer at Siebert Financial.

Markets have grown wary of cyclical spending and the methods hyperscalers are using to fund their AI buildouts.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average [(.DJI), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.DJI) rose 160.24 points, or 0.30%, to 53,577.40, the ​S&P 500 [(.SPX), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SPX) gained 24.38 points, or 0.32%, to 7,677.24 and the Nasdaq Composite [(.IXIC), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.IXIC) gained 171.11 points, or 0.66%, to 26,151.30.

## TECH STOCKS RECOVER

Most megacaps closed higher. ​Nvidia rose 2.2% and Meta [(META.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/META.O) climbed almost 2%. Chipmaker Micron [(MU.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/MU.O) gained 2.5%, while the broader chips index [(.SOX), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.SOX) ended 1.4% higher after a 2.7% fall on Monday.

Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, U.S., August 24, 2026. REUTERS/Brendan McDermid [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/traders-work-on-the-floor-of-the-nyse-in-new-york/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjI1TkE0V1hUSg%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Advanced Micro Devices [(AMD.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/AMD.O) rose 4.9% ‌after Raymond ⁠James upgraded the stock.

Advertisement · Scroll to continue

Shares of biotechnology firm Moderna [(MRNA.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/MRNA.O) surged 14% after Barclays hiked its target price.

The target price increase on Monday came days after Moderna and Merck [(MRK.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/MRK.N) reported late-stage trial results for their jointly developed skin cancer vaccine.

Dick's Sporting Goods [(DKS.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/DKS.N) plunged 30.7% after the retailer [cut its annual forecasts](https://www.reuters.com/business/dicks-sporting-goods-cuts-annual-forecasts-athleticwear-demand-weakens-2026-08-25/). Sportswear company Nike [(NKE.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/NKE.N) dipped.

Target [(TGT.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/TGT.N) shares fell 3.8% after the retailer apologized for and pulled a [Halloween costume criticized for evoking blackface](https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/target-shares-drop-5-after-halloween-costume-backlash-2026-08-25/), renewing concerns about brand missteps just as its financial turnaround effort had ​begun to gain traction.

The Personal Consumption ​Expenditures report on Wednesday could provide ⁠greater clarity on price pressures after an in-line consumer inflation reading this month tempered bets on an imminent interest-rate hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve.

On Tuesday, a survey showed U.S. consumer confidence [fell in August](https://www.reuters.com/business/us-consumer-confidence-falls-august-conference-board-says-2026-08-25/) to its lowest in seven ​months.

Still, money market participants are pricing in one 25-basis-point rate increase by the end of the year, according to ​LSEG data.

Against this backdrop, ⁠investors will watch Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole, Wyoming, speech on Friday for clues on the central bank's approach to monetary policy.

Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.71-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 190 new highs and 79 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 3,059 stocks rose and 1,740 fell as advancing issues ⁠outnumbered decliners ​by a 1.76-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 11 new 52-week highs and four new lows while ​the Nasdaq Composite recorded 105 new highs and 85 new lows.

Volume on U.S. exchanges was 14.32 billion shares, compared with the 16.4 billion average for the full session over the last 20 ​trading days.

Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, U.S., Aug. 24, 2026.

Brendan McDermid \| Reuters

The [S&P 500](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.SPX/) rose slightly Tuesday, as Treasury yields fell for a second day. A rally in semiconductor stocks lifted the [Nasdaq Composite](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.IXIC/).

The broader index gained 0.32% to close at 7,677.28, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.66% to 26,151.30. The [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.DJI/) was up 160.24 points, or 0.3%, to close at 53,577.40 and notch its third straight winning session.

Bond yields slid, with the benchmark [10-year Treasury](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/US10Y/) note yield falling more than 7 basis points to 4.625%. Yields also retreated Monday after [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/24/bessent-1-trillion-treasury-general-account-bond-buybacks.html) that the Treasury Department could use its $1 trillion General Account to fund bond repurchases. On Tuesday, [West Texas Intermediate crude futures](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/@CL.1/) dropped more than 3%.

Chip stocks rallied ahead of [Nvidia](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVDA/)’s results due out after the close on Wednesday. Shares of the Jensen Huang-helmed company were up 2%, snapping a seven-day decline. [Advanced Micro Devices](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AMD/) and [Micron Technology](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/MU/) added 4.9% and 2.5%, respectively.

Consumer names were a notable laggard, with shares of [Dick’s Sporting Goods](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/DKS/) plunging 30% following disappointing results. The sports equipment retailer posted its worst day on record. Other retailers such as [Walmart](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/WMT/) and [Target](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/TGT/) were also under pressure, falling 1% and nearly 4%, respectively.

Sentiment was hurt by a worse-than-expected consumer confidence reading and a worsening trade conflict between the U.S. and Canada. Consumer confidence edged lower in August and grew particularly downbeat about the look further down the road. The Conference Board’s [Consumer Confidence Index](https://www.conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence/) moved to 89.4, down 0.8 points and below the Dow Jones consensus for 90.2.

Canada on Tuesday [announced retaliatory tariffs](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/25/canada-trump-tariffs-trade-carney-leblanc.html) against the United States, with the government saying it will match the 50% levies that President Donald Trump imposed over the weekend “dollar for dollar.”

“So far, corporate conference calls have talked about a resilient consumer, so while the vibes may be sour, the spending has held up — and spending, not sentiment, is what shows up in corporate earnings. Markets can look past a bad mood. They can’t look past a consumer who actually stops spending,” said Bret Kenwell, eToro US investment analyst. “Investors won’t have to wait long for the next update, with tomorrow’s GDP and PCE inflation reports shedding further light on the economy.”

Investors are now awaiting the personal consumption expenditure price index reading for July out on Wednesday.

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh ends the week Friday with a speech at the Fed’s annual symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, a potentially market moving catalyst. His address comes the week after a Treasury Department [plan](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/treasury-announces-upscaled-buyback-operation-for-longer-term-debt-sending-yields-lower.html) to double the size of planned bond repurchases, part of an effort to tame long-dated Treasury yields.

9 Hours Ago

## Stocks end higher

Stocks finished Tuesday’s session in the green.

The [Dow](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.DJI/) and [S&P 500](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.SPX/) each added around 0.3%. The [Nasdaq Composite](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.IXIC/) jumped 0.7%.

_— Alex Harring_

9 Hours Ago

## Oil prices fall as U.S. shifts to economic pressure on Iran

Oil storage tanks at the Cushing crude oil storage terminal in Cushing, Oklahoma, US, on Thursday, June 18, 2026.

Nick Oxford \| Bloomberg \| Getty Images

Crude oil prices closed more than 3% lower Tuesday as the U.S. shifts to a strategy of economic pressure on Iran, easing market fears of a renewed war in the Persian Gulf.

[Brent futures](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/@LCO.1/), the international benchmark, dropped 3.9% to close at $88.58 per barrel. U.S. [West Texas Intermediate crude](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/@CL.1/) lost 3.1% to settle at $82.36 a barrel.

Prices have fallen more than 5% this week after the U.S. government [unveiled](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/25/us-iran-secondary-sanctions-china-india-uae-hormuz-trade-.html) a fresh raft of sanctions on Iran and so-called enablers that continue to trade with the Islamic Republic.

Iran and Oman, meanwhile, held talks Tuesday about establishing a temporary joint shipping route through Hormuz.

_— Spencer Kimball_

10 Hours Ago

## Look to some currencies and commodities amid greenback weakness, UBS says

Investors should look to specific currencies, commodities and gold with the [U.S. dollar under pressure](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/25/debasement-trade-debt-gold-bitcoin-dollar.html), according to UBS.

“As the long-term shift away from the \[U.S.\] dollar continues, we think exposure to gold, broad commodities, and select currencies can help support returns and manage portfolio risks,” Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi, the bank’s global head of equities, wrote in a Tuesday note. “An actively managed approach to commodities can also help investors navigate changing supply conditions, geopolitical risks, and shifts in market leadership.”

_— Alex Harring_

Super Heavy v3 Booster 20 hangs from the chop sticks at Pad 2 as it prepares to roll back to the SpaceX launch production facility in Starbase, Texas, U.S., July 17, 2026.

## Wells Fargo upgraded Shift4 Payments to overweight rating

Bloomberg \| Bloomberg \| Getty Images

Wells Fargo upgraded [Shift4 Payments](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/FOUR/) to overweight from equal weight on Tuesday, citing “improved set up” after the second quarter.

The analysts noted there is opportunity for material expansion for the company that provides software and payment processing solutions if investors trust increases in international expansion, improving Free Cash Flow generation and in strategic alternatives.

The analysts also increased the company’s price target to $59 from $55, implying a 22.9% increase from Monday’s close. Shares were up over 5.7% for Shift4 Payments following the upgrade.

_— Ananya Chetia_

12 Hours Ago

## Nvidia shares poised to snap losing streak

[Nvidia](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVDA/) shares are on track Tuesday to snap their longest losing streak in around four years.

Shares of the chipmaker climbed 1.5% in midday trading, which would mark its first winning day in eight. Nvidia last recorded seven consecutive down days in 2022.

Nvidia is set to report earnings after the bell Wednesday. Despite the recent drawdown, shares are up more than 13% in 2026.

## Canada announces retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% against U.S. goods

Dominic LeBlanc, Minister of Internal Trade of Canada speaking on CNBC’s Squawk Box on Aug. 25th, 2026.

CNBC

On Tuesday, Canada said it would slap retaliatory tariffs against the United States, applying to roughly $20 billion in goods.

The new tariffs, set to take effect on Sept. 8, would apply to more than 700 U.S. goods and range from 15% to 50%. These duties would target steel, aluminum, dairy, seafood and more.

Ottawa’s new levies come after the U.S. announced [additional 50% tariffs](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/20/trump-tariffs-canada-trade.html) on a variety of Canadian products, targeting motor vehicles, alcohol and dairy.

## The ‘debasement trade’ sees momentum following bond buyback operation announcement

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks during a press conference at the Cash Room of the Treasury Department in Washington, D.C., on Aug. 24, 2026.

The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. “The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the \[signaling\] effect was very powerful,” said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

On Monday, the U.S. [rolled out](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/24/trump-iran-economy-sanctions-china-bessent.html) a global sanctions plan that targets “enablers,” helping keep Tehran’s economy afloat.

_— Justina Lee_

Mon, Aug 24 20266:51 PM EDT

## Strengthen your portfolio with these moves as long-dated yields stay elevated, UBS says

Long-dated Treasury yields were still relatively high on Monday, but investors can take a few steps to bolster their portfolio for this runup in rates.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been working to calm higher yields in long-dated Treasurys, announcing last week it would at least double its buyback program. Though yields retreated briefly, they were still elevated on Monday, with the [10-year Treasury yield](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/US10Y/) last at 4.7%. Bond yields and prices move inversely to one another, and price swings related to rate fluctuations are more dramatic for long-dated issues.

The news isn’t all that bad for investors, according to a Monday note from UBS. “Over the longer term, initiatives that result in financial repression and artificially bring down yields should be favorable for equities, while gold would be another beneficiary of this scenario.”

The firm recommended that investors focus on quality bonds with short- to medium-term maturities, “as they are less susceptible to volatility at the long end of the curve.”

Investors should also stay in stocks. “While higher yields are typically a headwind for equities, we believe strong corporate earnings and expectations of further growth should continue to support global equities broadly,” UBS said.

Finally, investors should consider “a mid-single digit allocation” to gold, according to the firm. “As a non-fiat real asset, it can benefit when financial repression fuels fears of currency debasement,” UBS said.

## Stock futures open little changed

U.S. equity futures opened little changed on Monday night. [Futures](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/@DJ.1/) tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 40 points, or 0.07%. [S&P 500 futures](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/@SP.1/) edged higher by 0.09% and [Nasdaq 100 futures](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/@ND.1/) gained 0.1%.
